title: True or False: The Product Owner is responsible for ensuring that the Developers adhere to the Definition of Done. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done is a shared commitment within the Scrum Team, but it is the Developers who are responsible for adhering to it during the creation of Increments. “The Developers are required to conform to the Definition of Done.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Developers are responsible for adhering to the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: The Developers are responsible for ensuring that the work meets the Definition of Done.

title: During the Sprint, a major bug is identified that significantly affects the product’s performance. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to prioritize and address critical bugs within the current Sprint to ensure product quality. “Developers are responsible for turning Product Backlog items into Increments of value each Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Delay the bug fix to the next Sprint to keep the current Sprint on track.
explanation1: Incorrect: Critical bugs should be addressed immediately to maintain product quality.
answer2: Work with the Developers to prioritize and fix the bug within the current Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Addressing critical issues promptly ensures the product remains functional and reliable.
answer3: Ignore the bug to focus on new features.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring critical issues compromises the product’s integrity and stakeholder trust.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle the bug fix with the team.
explanation4: Incorrect: While the Scrum Master facilitates, the Product Owner manages prioritization in the Product Backlog.

title: The team is struggling to meet the Definition of Done consistently. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to understand why the Definition of Done is not being met and collaborate on solutions, ensuring the product maintains high quality. “If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Lower the Definition of Done to match the team's current performance level.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering the Definition of Done undermines product quality and does not address the root cause.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to identify and address issues preventing adherence to the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: Working with the team fosters a problem-solving approach to maintaining quality standards.
answer3: Ignore the issue as long as some value is delivered.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring quality issues compromises the product and erodes stakeholder trust.
answer4: Shift focus to quantity over quality to meet deadlines.
explanation4: Incorrect: Prioritizing speed over quality contradicts the principles of Scrum.

title: Which three practices support the Scrum Team in maintaining high transparency? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Transparency is maintained through visible tools like Task Boards, regular Sprint Reviews, and keeping the Product Backlog current and clear for all team members and stakeholders. “Transparency enables inspection. Inspection without transparency is misleading and wasteful.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Using a Task Board to visualize work in progress.
explanation1: Correct: A Task Board helps the team and stakeholders see the status of tasks at a glance, promoting transparency.
answer2: Conducting regular Sprint Reviews with stakeholders.
explanation2: Correct: Sprint Reviews allow the team to showcase completed work and gather feedback, ensuring visibility of progress.
answer3: Maintaining a clear and current Product Backlog.
explanation3: Correct: An up-to-date Product Backlog provides transparency about what work is planned and prioritized.
answer4: Keeping discussions private among team members only.
explanation4: Incorrect: Transparency requires open communication and visibility to stakeholders, not closed discussions.
answer5: Skipping Sprint Retrospectives if everything is on track.
explanation5: Incorrect: Retrospectives are vital for continuous improvement and should always be conducted.

title: Which three factors contribute most to the Scrum Team’s ability to self-manage effectively? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Self-management is supported by a clear Sprint Goal, cross-functional skills, and open communication within the team, enabling them to collaborate and adapt effectively. “Self-managing teams choose who, how, and when their work gets done.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: A clear understanding of the Sprint Goal and its importance.
explanation1: Correct: Knowing the Sprint Goal helps the team stay focused and make decisions that align with their objectives.
answer2: Cross-functional skills within the team.
explanation2: Correct: Cross-functionality ensures the team has all necessary skills to complete the work without outside help.
answer3: Open communication and a culture of mutual respect.
explanation3: Correct: Open communication and respect enable the team to collaborate effectively and manage their own work.
answer4: Direct supervision from the Scrum Master.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Team is self-managing and does not require direct supervision from the Scrum Master.
answer5: Detailed task assignments by the Product Owner.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Scrum Team decides how to accomplish their work and does not rely on task assignments from the Product Owner.

title: During the Daily Scrum, the Developers discuss a new approach to achieving the Sprint Goal. How should the Product Owner respond? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Developers should use the Daily Scrum to inspect and adapt their progress, adjusting their approach as necessary to meet the Sprint Goal. “The Daily Scrum is used to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Intervene and ensure the team sticks to the original plan.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Developers are empowered to adjust their approach during the Sprint to achieve the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Encourage the team to adapt their plan as needed to stay focused on the Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Correct: The Daily Scrum is for the Developers to inspect progress and adapt their work plan to meet the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to prevent changes to the plan mid-Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not control the team's planning adjustments.
answer4: Ignore the discussion as it is outside the Product Owner’s responsibilities.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should remain engaged to understand progress and support as needed.

title: During the Daily Scrum, the Developers identify a dependency that might delay their progress. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to assess and manage dependencies, ensuring that they do not impede progress toward the Sprint Goal. “The Daily Scrum is used to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ask the Scrum Master to resolve the dependency independently.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner should collaborate with the team to address dependencies impacting value delivery.
answer2: Work with the Developers to assess the impact of the dependency and adjust the Product Backlog if necessary.
explanation2: Correct: Managing dependencies proactively helps the team stay aligned with the Sprint Goal and adjust priorities if needed.
answer3: Ignore the dependency as it is a technical issue for the Developers to manage.
explanation3: Incorrect: Dependencies that impact value delivery require active management and adjustment of priorities by the Product Owner.
answer4: Delay action until the next Sprint Planning session to reassess priorities.
explanation4: Incorrect: Addressing dependencies promptly is crucial to maintaining progress and value delivery.

title: True or False: The Product Owner must be available to answer questions about Product Backlog items during the Sprint. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner plays a key role in clarifying Product Backlog items and should be available to support the Developers throughout the Sprint. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner should be available to clarify items, ensuring the team understands what needs to be delivered.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner’s availability is crucial to ensuring that the team has the information needed to work efficiently.

title: True or False: The Scrum Master is responsible for deciding the order of items in the Product Backlog. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner is accountable for managing the Product Backlog, including prioritizing items to maximize value. “The Product Owner is the sole person responsible for managing the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for ordering the Product Backlog based on value and priorities.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner manages the order of items in the Product Backlog based on value considerations.

title: Which two strategies should the Product Owner use to ensure the Product Backlog remains relevant and aligned with market needs? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should regularly engage stakeholders and use data-driven prioritization to keep the Product Backlog aligned with market needs and value delivery. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Only update the Backlog during formal Scrum events like Sprint Planning and Reviews.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should be continuously updated based on new information, not just during formal events.
answer2: Regularly engage with stakeholders to gather insights and adjust the Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Continuous engagement helps ensure the Backlog reflects the latest market needs and stakeholder feedback.
answer3: Use data-driven prioritization to focus on high-value items.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help prioritize items that deliver the most value and align with business goals.
answer4: Ignore minor feedback to maintain Backlog stability.
explanation4: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered to keep the Backlog adaptable and aligned with evolving needs.
answer5: Delegate Backlog updates to the Developers to maintain focus on high-priority tasks.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing and updating the Product Backlog.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take to maintain a Product Backlog that aligns with business objectives? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage stakeholders regularly and use data-driven prioritization to keep the Product Backlog aligned with business goals, maximizing value delivery. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Update the Product Backlog only during Sprint Planning and Review sessions.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should be continuously refined and updated, not only during formal Scrum events.
answer2: Engage with stakeholders regularly to gather feedback and ensure alignment with business goals.
explanation2: Correct: Regular engagement helps keep the Product Backlog relevant and aligned with current objectives.
answer3: Use data-driven prioritization to focus on high-impact work.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help maintain a Product Backlog that is aligned with delivering the most value.
answer4: Ignore feedback that does not align with the current Product Goal.
explanation4: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered to maintain an adaptable and responsive Product Backlog.
answer5: Delegate Backlog updates to the Developers to streamline the process.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for managing and updating the Product Backlog.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take to ensure the Product Backlog remains aligned with current market needs? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should regularly engage with stakeholders and use data-driven prioritization to keep the Product Backlog aligned with current market needs and value delivery. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Only update the Product Backlog during formal Scrum events like Sprint Planning.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should be continuously updated based on new insights, not just during formal events.
answer2: Engage regularly with stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust the Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: Regular engagement ensures the Product Backlog stays relevant and aligned with market conditions.
answer3: Use data-driven prioritization to focus on high-value items.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help keep the Product Backlog focused on the most impactful work.
answer4: Ignore minor feedback to maintain the Backlog’s current structure.
explanation4: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered to keep the Backlog adaptable and responsive to changes.
answer5: Delegate Backlog updates to the Developers to streamline the process.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for managing the Product Backlog and cannot delegate this responsibility.

title: Which three actions demonstrate effective Product Backlog refinement by the Product Owner? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Effective refinement involves ongoing collaboration, clear communication, and continuous prioritization to ensure the Product Backlog remains aligned with current goals and needs. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Delegating refinement entirely to the Scrum Master.
explanation1: Incorrect: Refinement is a collaborative effort between the Product Owner and the Developers, not solely delegated.
answer2: Clarifying requirements to ensure Backlog items are actionable.
explanation2: Correct: Clear requirements help the team understand what is needed, reducing ambiguity.
answer3: Breaking down large items into smaller, more manageable tasks.
explanation3: Correct: Decomposing complex items allows for better planning and execution within Sprints.
answer4: Regularly reprioritizing items based on new feedback and insights.
explanation4: Correct: Regular reprioritization ensures the Backlog reflects the latest needs and priorities.
answer5: Waiting until Sprint Planning to refine Backlog items.
explanation5: Incorrect: Refinement is an ongoing activity, not limited to Sprint Planning sessions.

title: Which three actions best demonstrate the Product Owner’s involvement in maximizing value delivery during a Sprint? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner maximizes value delivery by collaborating with Developers, using stakeholder feedback, and regularly reviewing progress to ensure alignment with the Product Goal. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Directing the Developers on how to complete their tasks.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner does not direct the Developers’ work but collaborates to ensure alignment with the Product Goal.
answer2: Collaborating with the Developers to refine and prioritize work during the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Ongoing collaboration ensures that the highest value work is prioritized and refined appropriately.
answer3: Using stakeholder feedback to adjust priorities in the Product Backlog.
explanation3: Correct: Managing stakeholder feedback helps ensure the Backlog reflects current needs and maximizes value delivery.
answer4: Regularly reviewing progress to ensure that work aligns with the Product Goal.
explanation4: Correct: Regular reviews help ensure that work remains aligned with the overall objectives and value delivery.
answer5: Waiting until the Sprint Review to make any adjustments to priorities.
explanation5: Incorrect: Continuous refinement and prioritization throughout the Sprint help maintain alignment and responsiveness.

title: A stakeholder approaches the Product Owner with a new urgent requirement mid-Sprint. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: New requirements should be added to the Product Backlog and prioritized accordingly, not added mid-Sprint. This ensures the team remains focused on the current Sprint Goal. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately add the requirement to the current Sprint Backlog.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changes to the Sprint Backlog should be avoided during the Sprint.
answer2: Discuss the new requirement with the team and adjust the Sprint Goal accordingly.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal should not be adjusted once the Sprint has started.
answer3: Add the requirement to the Product Backlog and prioritize it for the next Sprint.
explanation3: Correct: The Product Owner manages the Product Backlog and prioritizes new work for future Sprints.
answer4: Ignore the request and focus on the current Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: Ignoring stakeholder feedback is not recommended, but it should be managed appropriately.

title: During a Sprint, the Product Owner notices that a key feature is missing from the Increment. What is the most appropriate action? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: If a feature is missing, it should be documented and prioritized in the Product Backlog. The Product Owner ensures the Backlog reflects the highest value work. “The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately ask the Developers to add the feature during the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding work during the Sprint disrupts the Sprint Goal and focus.
answer2: Document the missing feature and prioritize it in the Product Backlog for the next Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Missing features should be managed in the Product Backlog and prioritized accordingly.
answer3: Escalate the issue to the Scrum Master to address immediately.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not manage Product Backlog items.
answer4: Extend the Sprint duration to complete the missing feature.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprint durations are fixed and should not be extended.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies frequent misunderstandings of Product Backlog items as a major impediment. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to enhance the refinement process, ensuring Product Backlog items are clear, actionable, and ready for future Sprints. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the feedback and focus on other improvements.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback undermines the team’s ability to address key impediments to progress.
answer2: Work with the Developers to improve the clarity of Backlog items during refinement sessions.
explanation2: Correct: Improving refinement helps ensure that Product Backlog items are actionable and align with team understanding.
answer3: Delegate the responsibility of refinement to the Scrum Master.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner should be actively involved in refinement and clarity of the Product Backlog items.
answer4: Delay addressing these issues until the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement should be continuously improved, not delayed.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is responsible for ordering the Product Backlog in a way that maximizes the team's efficiency. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner focuses on maximizing product value, which may not always align directly with maximizing team efficiency. Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: While efficiency is important, the main responsibility is to maximize product value, not just team efficiency.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner's main responsibility is to maximize the value of the product, not team efficiency.

title: True or False: The Scrum Master is responsible for deciding which Product Backlog items are included in the Sprint. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner and Developers work together during Sprint Planning to determine which Product Backlog items will be included in the Sprint, guided by the Sprint Goal. “The Scrum Team selects items from the Product Backlog to include in the current Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not decide the content of the Sprint Backlog; this is a joint decision involving the Product Owner and Developers.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner and Developers collaboratively decide on the Sprint Backlog during Sprint Planning.

title: Which two elements are critical for the Scrum Master to support the Development Team effectively? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master supports the Development Team by facilitating Scrum events and removing impediments, enabling the team to work efficiently and effectively. “The Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum Team’s effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Facilitating Scrum events to ensure they are productive.
explanation1: Correct: Facilitating events helps ensure that the team stays on track and follows Scrum practices effectively.
answer2: Removing impediments that hinder the team’s progress.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team by removing obstacles that block progress, allowing the team to focus on their work.
answer3: Assigning tasks to the team members based on their skills.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Development Team self-organizes and decides how to accomplish their work.
answer4: Tracking the team’s performance metrics closely.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master supports team effectiveness but does not manage performance metrics in a traditional sense.
answer5: Approving the team’s work before it is presented in the Sprint Review.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for assessing the Increment, not the Scrum Master.

title: Which three responsibilities are unique to the Product Owner within the Scrum Team? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner is responsible for prioritizing the Product Backlog, communicating clearly with the team, and managing stakeholder expectations, ensuring value-driven development. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Prioritizing Product Backlog items based on business value and stakeholder input.
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner ensures that the most valuable and impactful items are prioritized.
answer2: Clearly communicating Product Backlog items to the Development Team.
explanation2: Correct: Clear communication ensures that the team understands the requirements and priorities.
answer3: Managing stakeholder expectations and incorporating feedback into the Product Backlog.
explanation3: Correct: Managing stakeholder expectations and refining the Product Backlog ensures the product delivers maximum value.
answer4: Facilitating Daily Scrums to keep the team aligned.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates events, not the Product Owner.
answer5: Approving work before it is considered done.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Definition of Done determines completeness, not approval by the Product Owner.

title: Which two responsibilities does the Product Owner hold during a Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner engages stakeholders, gathers feedback, and refines the Product Backlog to maximize the product's value. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ensuring that all tasks are completed on time.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Developers manage the progress of their work.
answer2: Managing stakeholder expectations and gathering feedback.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner engages with stakeholders to ensure the product meets expectations.
answer3: Attending the Daily Scrum to monitor progress closely.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner does not need to attend the Daily Scrum regularly.
answer4: Adjusting the Product Backlog as new information emerges.
explanation4: Correct: The Product Owner continuously refines the Backlog based on feedback and changing conditions.
answer5: Delegating refinement activities to the Scrum Master.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for refinement and cannot delegate this task.

title: During the Sprint, the team realizes they are consistently missing their Sprint Goal. What should the Scrum Master do to help the team? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should use the Sprint Retrospective to facilitate a discussion about why the Sprint Goal is being missed and identify improvements for future Sprints. “The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to improve processes and quality.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Extend the Sprint duration to complete all tasks.
explanation1: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint violates Scrum’s time-boxing principle and does not solve the underlying issues.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion during the Sprint Retrospective to identify root causes and solutions.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Retrospective allows the team to reflect, identify challenges, and make adjustments for future Sprints.
answer3: Reassign tasks to ensure all work is completed on time.
explanation3: Incorrect: Task reassignment disrupts self-management and does not address the root causes of missed goals.
answer4: Report the issue to upper management for guidance.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Team is self-managing and responsible for resolving its own challenges.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Product Owner is unavailable. What should the Scrum Team do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: In the absence of the Product Owner, the Scrum Team should proceed with what they have and make alignment adjustments later. Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Postpone the Sprint Planning until the Product Owner is available.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner's absence should not delay the Scrum Team's progress.
answer2: Proceed with the Sprint Planning and make decisions based on the current Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: The Developers can proceed with available information and align with the Product Owner later.
answer3: Cancel the Sprint until the Product Owner is available.
explanation3: Incorrect: Cancelling the Sprint disrupts the flow of the Scrum Team.
answer4: Wait for the Product Owner and reschedule all upcoming events.
explanation4: Incorrect: Rescheduling disrupts the team's work cadence.

title: True or False: The Product Owner has the final say on the Definition of Done. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done is established by the entire Scrum Team to ensure quality and consistency across all work. “The Definition of Done is created by the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is defined by the entire Scrum Team, not solely by the Product Owner.
explanation2: Correct: The Definition of Done is collaboratively created and agreed upon by the Scrum Team.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take if the team consistently misses the Definition of Done? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to understand challenges and refine Backlog items, ensuring quality standards are consistently met. “If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Adjust the Definition of Done to lower quality standards.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering quality standards compromises the integrity of the product and does not address the root issues.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to understand obstacles and refine the Backlog items.
explanation2: Correct: Collaboration helps identify and address obstacles, ensuring that items meet the Definition of Done.
answer3: Reassign incomplete work to the next Sprint without refinement.
explanation3: Incorrect: Moving work forward without addressing issues can lead to repeated failures.
answer4: Improve refinement practices to ensure items are better understood and actionable.
explanation4: Correct: Effective refinement helps ensure that items are clear, manageable, and meet the Definition of Done.
answer5: Ignore the issue as long as some value is delivered.
explanation5: Incorrect: Ignoring quality issues undermines the product’s value and consistency.

title: Which two elements are crucial to ensure that the Product Backlog remains relevant and useful? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Regular refinement and incorporating stakeholder feedback are critical for maintaining a Product Backlog that accurately reflects priorities and business needs. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Regular Backlog Refinement sessions
explanation1: Correct: Refinement sessions help keep the Product Backlog up-to-date and ensure items are clearly understood.
answer2: Active involvement of the Scrum Master in prioritizing tasks
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for prioritizing tasks, not the Scrum Master.
answer3: Frequent updates to reflect stakeholder feedback
explanation3: Correct: Regular updates ensure that the Product Backlog reflects current priorities and stakeholder needs.
answer4: A fixed Backlog that does not change during Sprints
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Backlog is dynamic and should be updated as new information becomes available.
answer5: Focus on technical tasks over business value
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should prioritize business value, not just technical tasks.

title: The team consistently struggles to complete all tasks within the Sprint. Which Scrum artifact can help them improve their planning and focus? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog helps the Development Team manage their tasks by providing a clear view of what work needs to be done to achieve the Sprint Goal. “The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog lists all future work but does not directly help manage the current Sprint’s workload.
answer2: Sprint Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Backlog provides a clear view of the work the team has committed to, helping them manage their tasks and maintain focus.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment shows what has been completed but does not help plan or manage tasks.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done sets quality standards but does not aid in workload management.

title: Which artifact embodies the Scrum value of transparency by showing what work has been completed? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Increment embodies transparency by clearly showing what work has been completed, providing visibility into the team’s progress toward the Product Goal. “An Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog lists future work, not what has been completed.
answer2: Increment
explanation2: Correct: The Increment demonstrates completed work and embodies transparency by showing progress.
answer3: Sprint Backlog
explanation3: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog shows current work in progress but not completed work.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done defines quality but does not demonstrate completed work.

title: Which artifact provides transparency into the current progress and helps guide the team’s inspection during the Sprint? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog provides transparency into the team’s current progress, helping guide inspections and adaptations during the Sprint. “The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog contains all future work and does not provide direct visibility into the current progress.
answer2: Sprint Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Backlog provides a transparent view of current progress and guides the team during inspection.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment shows completed work but does not directly guide inspection during the Sprint.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures quality but does not directly provide progress visibility.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is required to attend every Daily Scrum to stay updated on the team's progress.
feedback: The Daily Scrum is a developer-focused event meant for team synchronization rather than Product Owner oversight. Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner does not need to attend Daily Scrums; the event is for Developers to synchronize their work.
explanation2: Correct: The Daily Scrum is for Developers to inspect progress towards the Sprint Goal, not for the Product Owner's updates.

title: True or False: The Sprint Review is primarily an opportunity for the Product Owner to demonstrate the Increment to stakeholders. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Review is a collaborative event that involves the entire Scrum Team and stakeholders to inspect the Increment and plan future adaptations. “The Scrum Team and stakeholders collaborate about what was done in the Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is a collaborative event where the entire Scrum Team and stakeholders inspect the Increment and discuss next steps.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Review involves the whole Scrum Team and stakeholders, focusing on collaboration and inspection of the Increment.

title: Which three practices support effective Sprint Planning? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Effective Sprint Planning involves setting a clear Sprint Goal, collaborating with the entire team, and reviewing past performance to guide realistic commitments. “Sprint Planning initiates the Sprint by laying out the work to be performed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Setting a clear and realistic Sprint Goal that aligns with the Product Backlog priorities.
explanation1: Correct: A clear Sprint Goal provides focus and guides the team throughout the Sprint.
answer2: Ensuring the entire Scrum Team collaborates during the planning session.
explanation2: Correct: Collaboration ensures that the team is aligned on what can be achieved in the Sprint.
answer3: Reviewing past Sprint performance to inform planning decisions.
explanation3: Correct: Analyzing past performance helps the team set realistic goals and make informed planning decisions.
answer4: Allowing the Product Owner to assign tasks to team members.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Development Team is self-managing and decides who will work on which tasks.
answer5: Planning the work without input from the Development Team to save time.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Development Team’s input is critical to realistic and achievable Sprint Planning.

title: Which three elements are crucial for effective Sprint Planning? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Effective Sprint Planning relies on setting a clear Sprint Goal, understanding priorities with the Product Owner, and estimating capacity accurately to ensure achievable commitments. “Sprint Planning initiates the Sprint by laying out the work to be performed for the Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: A clearly defined Sprint Goal that guides the work.
explanation1: Correct: The Sprint Goal provides a clear objective and focus for the Sprint.
answer2: A complete and detailed list of tasks for each team member.
explanation2: Incorrect: Scrum does not require detailed task assignments during planning; the team self-organizes.
answer3: Input from the Product Owner on priority and value of work items.
explanation3: Correct: The Product Owner’s input ensures that the most valuable work is included in the Sprint.
answer4: Accurate capacity estimates based on the team’s past performance.
explanation4: Correct: Capacity estimates help the team commit to a realistic amount of work for the Sprint.
answer5: Approval from the Scrum Master to begin work.
explanation5: Incorrect: Approval is not required; the team starts work once the plan is agreed upon.

title: During a Sprint Review, the stakeholders suggest changes that were not anticipated by the Scrum Team. What is the best approach to handle this feedback? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Team should capture stakeholder feedback during the Sprint Review and update the Product Backlog to consider these changes in future Sprints. “The Sprint Review is a working session, and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the feedback and focus on the work already planned.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring stakeholder feedback undermines collaboration and the value of the Sprint Review.
answer2: Capture the feedback and update the Product Backlog for future consideration.
explanation2: Correct: Feedback should be used to refine the Product Backlog, guiding future work and ensuring alignment with stakeholder needs.
answer3: Incorporate the changes immediately into the current Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Mid-Sprint changes disrupt focus and are not part of the Sprint Review process.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to prioritize the changes in the current Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: Prioritization is managed by the Product Owner and should be planned for future Sprints, not the current one.

title: The Development Team realizes that a critical feature was misunderstood during Sprint Planning, affecting the Sprint Goal. What should they do next? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: When misunderstandings about a feature arise, the Development Team should work with the Product Owner to clarify and adjust their approach, keeping aligned with the Sprint Goal. “During the Sprint, scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Continue working as planned to avoid wasting time.
explanation1: Incorrect: Continuing without addressing misunderstandings can lead to ineffective work and missed goals.
answer2: Discuss the issue with the Product Owner and adjust the Sprint Backlog if needed.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should clarify the feature, and the team should adapt their Sprint Backlog to align with the correct understanding.
answer3: Escalate the issue to the Scrum Master for resolution.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Development Team and Product Owner should collaborate directly to resolve such misunderstandings.
answer4: Cancel the Sprint and start over with a new plan.
explanation4: Incorrect: Cancelling the Sprint is a last resort and not typically necessary for misunderstandings that can be clarified.

title: The Product Owner notices that the Development Team is not meeting the Definition of Done. What should be the immediate next step? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Addressing adherence to the Definition of Done during the Retrospective allows the team to collaboratively identify and commit to improvements. “The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity to improve quality and effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the issue and focus on the next Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring quality standards leads to inconsistent Increments and potential rework.
answer2: Discuss the importance of the Definition of Done during the Sprint Retrospective.
explanation2: Correct: The Retrospective allows the team to reflect on quality issues and agree on improvements.
answer3: Request the Scrum Master to enforce quality standards.
explanation3: Incorrect: Enforcing standards is not the role of the Scrum Master; it’s a team responsibility.
answer4: Reduce the Definition of Done requirements temporarily.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reducing quality standards compromises the integrity of the Increment and the Scrum process.

title: Which pillar of Scrum is primarily responsible for enabling the team to assess progress toward the Product Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Inspection is essential for assessing progress toward the Product Goal, allowing the team to make informed decisions. “The Scrum Team inspects progress toward the Product Goal to detect undesirable variances.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Inspection
explanation1: Correct: Inspection allows the team to regularly assess their progress toward the Product Goal.
answer2: Adaptation
explanation2: Incorrect: Adaptation occurs after Inspection, once progress has been assessed.
answer3: Transparency
explanation3: Incorrect: Transparency provides visibility, but Inspection specifically involves assessing progress.
answer4: Respect
explanation4: Incorrect: Respect is a Scrum value, not a pillar that involves assessing progress.

title: Which two pillars are directly involved when the team identifies a problem and decides to change their approach? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Inspection identifies problems within the team's work, and Adaptation allows them to adjust their approach accordingly. “Adaptation becomes more difficult when the people involved are not empowered.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Inspection and Transparency
explanation1: Incorrect: Transparency makes the problem visible, but Adaptation is necessary to change the approach.
answer2: Inspection and Adaptation
explanation2: Correct: Inspection identifies the problem, and Adaptation allows the team to change their approach.
answer3: Transparency and Adaptation
explanation3: Incorrect: Transparency helps identify problems, but Inspection is needed before adaptation.
answer4: Respect and Adaptation
explanation4: Incorrect: Respect fosters collaboration, but Inspection is required to identify problems.
answer5: Adaptation and Focus
explanation5: Incorrect: Focus maintains direction, but Inspection is needed to identify when a change is required.

title: Which two strategies can help the Development Team manage unexpected impediments during the Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Managing impediments effectively involves discussing them during the Daily Scrum and leveraging the Scrum Master’s support to facilitate quick resolutions. “The Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum Team’s effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Address impediments during the Daily Scrum to adapt the plan as needed.
explanation1: Correct: The Daily Scrum provides an opportunity to discuss impediments and adjust plans to stay on track toward the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Engage the Scrum Master to help remove impediments quickly.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master plays a crucial role in facilitating the removal of obstacles that impede the team’s progress.
answer3: Skip the Daily Scrum to focus directly on solving the impediments.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is essential for maintaining transparency and should not be skipped.
answer4: Delegate impediment resolution to the most senior team member.
explanation4: Incorrect: Impediment resolution is a team effort, facilitated by the Scrum Master, not an individual task.
answer5: Extend the Sprint to make up for time lost due to impediments.
explanation5: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint is against Scrum principles and disrupts the time-box.

title: Which two techniques can help the Development Team maintain focus and manage their work effectively during a Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Daily Scrums and Task Boards are effective tools that help the Development Team stay focused, inspect progress, and adapt their work to meet the Sprint Goal. “The Daily Scrum is used to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Daily Scrums focused on inspecting progress and adapting the plan.
explanation1: Correct: The Daily Scrum helps the team stay on track by inspecting progress and adapting the plan as needed.
answer2: Updating the Sprint Backlog with new tasks daily.
explanation2: Incorrect: New tasks should not be added without careful consideration of their impact on the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Using a visible Task Board to track work in progress.
explanation3: Correct: A Task Board provides a clear visual representation of task status, helping the team stay focused and organized.
answer4: Skipping Retrospectives to save time for task completion.
explanation4: Incorrect: Retrospectives are essential for continuous improvement and should not be skipped.
answer5: Reassigning tasks frequently to balance workload.
explanation5: Incorrect: Frequent task reassignments disrupt flow and can confuse team dynamics.

title: During a Sprint, the team realizes that the work remaining is not decreasing as expected according to the Burndown Chart. What should the team focus on to resolve this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Daily Scrum provides an opportunity for the team to inspect progress, identify impediments, and adapt their plan to ensure they continue moving toward the Sprint Goal. “The Daily Scrum is used to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Adding more resources to speed up progress.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding resources mid-Sprint disrupts the team's dynamics and does not address underlying issues.
answer2: Identifying impediments and adapting their plan during the Daily Scrum.
explanation2: Correct: The Daily Scrum helps the team identify issues and adapt their work to stay on track with the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Requesting an extension of the Sprint to finish the work.
explanation3: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint goes against Scrum principles and does not resolve the core problem.
answer4: Reprioritizing tasks to focus on easier ones.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reprioritizing for easier tasks avoids addressing real impediments and does not support the Sprint Goal.

title: During the Sprint, the Product Owner frequently changes priorities, leading to confusion among the Development Team. How should the team address this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Retrospective provides an opportunity to address recurring issues like changing priorities, allowing the team and Product Owner to agree on a better approach. “The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to improve processes.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Discuss the issue in the Daily Scrum and adapt as needed.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal and is not the place to manage priority changes.
answer2: Raise the issue in the Sprint Retrospective and agree on a clearer process for handling mid-Sprint changes.
explanation2: Correct: The Retrospective is an appropriate setting to discuss process improvements and agree on how to handle changes in priority.
answer3: Ignore the changes and continue with the original plan.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring changes does not address the underlying issue and could lead to misalignment.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to enforce the current priorities.
explanation4: Incorrect: Enforcing priorities is not the Scrum Master’s role; it requires a collaborative approach between the team and the Product Owner.

title: The Development Team is struggling to manage their workload, with some members frequently overwhelmed while others are underutilized. Which tool or technique could help address this issue? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: A Task Board helps the team visualize task distribution and identify imbalances, allowing them to self-organize and adjust workloads as needed. “Task Boards can enhance transparency and provide clear insights into progress.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Velocity Tracking
explanation1: Incorrect: Velocity measures past performance but does not balance workload within the team.
answer2: Task Board
explanation2: Correct: A Task Board helps visualize the distribution of tasks, enabling the team to balance workload effectively.
answer3: Sprint Review
explanation3: Incorrect: The Sprint Review assesses the completed work and does not help manage team workload.
answer4: Burndown Chart
explanation4: Incorrect: The Burndown Chart tracks overall progress but does not provide insights into individual workload distribution.

title: The team consistently underestimates the time required for their tasks, leading to incomplete work at the end of Sprints. Which Scrum artifact can help improve their estimation accuracy? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Velocity Tracking helps teams understand their capacity based on historical data, allowing them to make more accurate estimates for future Sprints. “Velocity is an optional but useful tool to help understand team performance.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog lists planned work but does not directly aid in improving estimation accuracy.
answer2: Velocity Tracking
explanation2: Correct: Velocity Tracking provides insights into the team’s actual performance over multiple Sprints, helping improve future estimations.
answer3: Daily Scrum
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum focuses on inspecting progress but does not help directly with estimation improvements.
answer4: Burndown Chart
explanation4: Incorrect: The Burndown Chart tracks progress within the Sprint but does not address estimation accuracy.

title: Which Scrum value is most demonstrated when the team faces a challenge and adapts their strategy to stay aligned with the Sprint Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Courage is demonstrated when the team adapts their strategy in response to challenges, empowering them to make bold decisions to achieve the Sprint Goal. “Scrum’s success is based on people becoming more proficient in living five values.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Courage
explanation1: Correct: Courage enables the team to take bold actions and adapt their strategy when faced with challenges.
answer2: Openness
explanation2: Incorrect: Openness supports transparency but does not directly drive the adaptation of strategies.
answer3: Respect
explanation3: Incorrect: Respect fosters collaboration, but Courage is needed to confront and address challenges.
answer4: Focus
explanation4: Incorrect: Focus helps maintain alignment, but Courage drives the willingness to adapt.

title: True or False: The Product Owner has the authority to change Sprint Goals as they see fit. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Goal provides a shared focus for the team during the Sprint and should not be altered without careful consideration of its impact. “The Sprint Goal is the single objective for the Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: Once set, Sprint Goals should remain stable to maintain focus and direction during the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Goal is set during Sprint Planning and should remain unchanged to guide the team’s work.

title: True or False: The Product Owner has the authority to change the Sprint Goal during the Sprint if new priorities emerge. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Goal provides a shared focus for the team and should not be changed during the Sprint. Any adjustments should be made in future Sprints. “The Sprint Goal is the single objective for the Sprint.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: Changing the Sprint Goal disrupts the focus and alignment of the team.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Goal is set during Sprint Planning and should remain stable to guide the team’s efforts.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers express concerns that the planned work may exceed their capacity. What is the best action for the Product Owner? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog, ensuring the team commits to achievable work that maximizes value. “Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Push the team to commit to the planned work to maximize output.
explanation1: Incorrect: Overcommitting can lead to unmet goals and team burnout.
answer2: Work with the team to adjust the Sprint Backlog, focusing on high-value items that align with the Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Sprint Backlog ensures commitments are achievable and aligned with value delivery.
answer3: Ignore the concerns and maintain the current Sprint plan.
explanation3: Incorrect: Addressing team concerns helps maintain sustainable progress and morale.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to manage the team’s workload.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should actively participate in managing work scope and priorities with the Developers.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers identify that the scope of the Sprint Goal may be too ambitious. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog, ensuring that the team remains focused on the most valuable and achievable work. “Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Encourage the team to commit to the Sprint Goal regardless of the challenges.
explanation1: Incorrect: Committing to unrealistic goals can lead to burnout and unmet Sprint outcomes.
answer2: Collaborate with the team to adjust the Sprint Backlog, focusing on the most valuable work.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Sprint Backlog helps align the team’s efforts with achievable, high-value outcomes.
answer3: Delay the Sprint to reevaluate the Sprint Goal and items.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying the Sprint disrupts the cadence and flow of work in Scrum.
answer4: Reassign some work to another team to meet the Sprint Goal.
explanation4: Incorrect: Reassigning work undermines team accountability and focus.

title: During the Sprint, the Developers identify that they have underestimated the complexity of a Backlog item. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog, ensuring the team remains focused on delivering value without compromising quality. “Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ask the team to complete it anyway to stay on schedule.
explanation1: Incorrect: Forcing completion of underestimated work can lead to poor quality and unmet Sprint Goals.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to adjust the Sprint Backlog and refine the item for future Sprints if necessary.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the Backlog ensures the team can focus on achievable work and maintain quality.
answer3: Ignore the issue and let the team handle it independently.
explanation3: Incorrect: Collaboration helps ensure that the Sprint remains focused and valuable, even when challenges arise.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to extend the Sprint to allow more time for the item.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints cannot be extended; adjustments should be made to the Sprint Backlog instead.

title: During Sprint Planning, the team discovers that some selected Product Backlog items are unclear. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to refine unclear items, ensuring they are clear and actionable before being included in the Sprint. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Include the items anyway and clarify them during the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Including unclear items can disrupt the Sprint and increase uncertainty.
answer2: Work with the Developers to refine the items immediately, ensuring they are ready for the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Refining items ensures they are clear, actionable, and ready for the Sprint, reducing confusion.
answer3: Move the items to the next Sprint to refine them later.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying unclear work without refinement does not address the underlying issues.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to lead additional refinement sessions.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner leads refinement efforts with the team’s collaboration.

title: During the Sprint Review, stakeholders express dissatisfaction with the product’s progress. What is the best action for the Product Owner? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should engage with stakeholders during the Sprint Review to gather feedback and update the Product Backlog, ensuring future work aligns with stakeholder expectations. “The purpose of the Sprint Review is to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Defend the team’s work and explain the challenges they faced.
explanation1: Incorrect: Defending work without addressing feedback does not help improve future iterations.
answer2: Engage with stakeholders to understand their feedback and adjust the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should actively manage stakeholder feedback and refine the Backlog to align with needs.
answer3: Ignore the feedback and continue with the planned Backlog items.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback undermines the purpose of the Sprint Review and stakeholder engagement.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle stakeholder concerns separately.
explanation4: Incorrect: Managing stakeholder expectations is the responsibility of the Product Owner.

title: During the Sprint Review, stakeholders suggest changes that could impact the Product Goal. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should assess stakeholder feedback collaboratively with the Scrum Team to determine the impact on the Product Goal and adjust the Product Backlog as necessary. “The Sprint Review is an opportunity to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately change the Product Goal to align with stakeholder requests.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changing the Product Goal without evaluation can disrupt the product’s strategic direction.
answer2: Engage stakeholders in a discussion with the Scrum Team to evaluate the impact of the suggested changes.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should facilitate discussions to assess feedback and adjust the Product Backlog as needed.
answer3: Reject the suggestions to maintain the current Product Goal.
explanation3: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered and evaluated to keep the Product Backlog relevant.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle the stakeholder feedback separately.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing feedback and refining the Product Backlog.

title: Which three actions best demonstrate the Product Owner’s responsibility in managing stakeholder expectations? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should regularly engage stakeholders, use data to inform decisions, and set clear expectations to manage relationships effectively. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Only communicate with stakeholders during formal Scrum events.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ongoing communication is key to managing expectations effectively.
answer2: Engage stakeholders regularly to gather feedback and adjust the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Regular engagement helps keep the Backlog aligned with stakeholder needs.
answer3: Use data and metrics to explain prioritization decisions.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven prioritization builds trust and transparency with stakeholders.
answer4: Set clear expectations about what can and cannot be achieved within the current Sprint.
explanation4: Correct: Clear communication helps stakeholders understand the team’s focus and constraints.
answer5: Delegate communication with stakeholders to the Scrum Master.
explanation5: Incorrect: Managing stakeholder relationships is a key responsibility of the Product Owner.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take when stakeholders frequently request changes during a Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should evaluate stakeholder requests, manage them through the Product Backlog, and communicate how changes impact the current Sprint, maintaining alignment and focus. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Accept all changes to keep stakeholders happy.
explanation1: Incorrect: Accepting changes mid-Sprint disrupts focus and undermines the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Evaluate the changes and incorporate them into the Product Backlog for future prioritization.
explanation2: Correct: Managing new requests through the Product Backlog ensures the team maintains focus on the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Communicate the impact of changes on the Sprint Goal to stakeholders.
explanation3: Correct: Transparent communication helps stakeholders understand the consequences of their requests.
answer4: Extend the Sprint to accommodate the changes.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprint durations are fixed and should not be extended.
answer5: Delegate stakeholder management to the Scrum Master to avoid disruptions.
explanation5: Incorrect: Managing stakeholder expectations is the responsibility of the Product Owner.

title: Which two actions are important for the Product Owner when multiple Scrum Teams are working on the same product? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: When multiple teams work on the same product, the Product Owner must coordinate and manage dependencies to ensure all teams are aligned with the product vision. “Multiple Scrum Teams often work together on the same product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ensure each team has a separate Product Backlog.
explanation1: Incorrect: All teams work from a single, unified Product Backlog managed by the Product Owner.
answer2: Facilitate communication between teams to ensure alignment.
explanation2: Correct: Coordination helps prevent duplication and ensures teams work towards a shared goal.
answer3: Adjust priorities regularly to manage dependencies between teams.
explanation3: Correct: Regular adjustments help keep all teams aligned and focused on delivering value.
answer4: Delegate Backlog management to the Scrum Master for each team.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner maintains responsibility for the entire Product Backlog.
answer5: Set different goals for each team to maximize output.
explanation5: Incorrect: Teams should work towards shared goals to ensure coherent progress.

title: Which three actions should the Development Team take to ensure they meet the Definition of Done? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Reviewing the Definition of Done, continuous testing, and conducting code reviews help ensure that the Development Team meets quality standards and produces a shippable Increment. “The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Review the Definition of Done during Sprint Planning.
explanation1: Correct: Reviewing the Definition of Done helps the team understand the quality criteria that need to be met.
answer2: Test and integrate work continuously during the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Continuous testing and integration help catch defects early and ensure the work meets quality standards.
answer3: Seek approval from the Product Owner before marking work as done.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner does not approve tasks; the Definition of Done guides when work is complete.
answer4: Conduct code reviews among team members.
explanation4: Correct: Code reviews help ensure that the work meets quality standards and conforms to the Definition of Done.
answer5: Rely solely on automated testing at the end of the Sprint.
explanation5: Incorrect: Relying only on end-of-Sprint testing increases the risk of defects and does not guarantee adherence to the Definition of Done.

title: During a Sprint, the Developers identify a high-priority bug that impacts the product’s usability. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to prioritize and fix critical bugs within the current Sprint, maintaining product integrity. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the bug and continue with the planned work.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring critical issues can harm product quality and stakeholder satisfaction.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to prioritize the bug fix within the current Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: Addressing critical bugs promptly ensures the product remains functional and valuable.
answer3: Delay the fix until the next Sprint to maintain the current focus.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying fixes for critical bugs can lead to further problems and technical debt.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle the bug independently.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should be involved in prioritizing critical issues, although the Scrum Master can facilitate.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies recurring issues with unclear requirements for Product Backlog items. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should actively engage in refining Backlog items with the team, ensuring clarity and understanding to enhance future Sprint success. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the feedback to maintain the current refinement process.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback prevents improvement and does not address recurring issues.
answer2: Work with the team to improve the refinement process, ensuring requirements are clear and well understood.
explanation2: Correct: Improving refinement processes helps ensure that Backlog items are actionable and reduce misunderstandings.
answer3: Delegate the responsibility of clarifying requirements to the Scrum Master.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner plays a key role in refinement and must actively participate in clarifying requirements.
answer4: Delay addressing these issues until the next formal refinement session.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement improvements should be addressed continuously, not delayed.

title: During the Sprint Review, stakeholders suggest changes to the Product Goal based on market shifts. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should assess feedback collaboratively with the Scrum Team to determine its impact on the Product Backlog and Product Goal. “The Product Owner is responsible for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Immediately change the Product Goal to align with stakeholder feedback.
explanation1: Incorrect: Changes to the Product Goal should be carefully considered and not made impulsively.
answer2: Discuss the feedback with the Scrum Team and stakeholders to assess the impact on the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner should collaborate to evaluate changes and adjust the Backlog accordingly.
answer3: Ignore the feedback and focus on the current Sprint Goal.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback undermines stakeholder trust and product value.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to handle stakeholder concerns separately.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing the Product Goal and adjusting the Backlog based on feedback.

title: Stakeholders are frequently requesting changes to the Product Backlog. How should the Product Owner manage these requests? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should evaluate stakeholder requests based on value and prioritize them in the Product Backlog to ensure the team is focused on the most impactful work. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Accept all requests to keep stakeholders satisfied.
explanation1: Incorrect: Accepting all requests without prioritization can lead to an unfocused Backlog.
answer2: Evaluate each request based on its potential value and prioritize accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner must balance stakeholder requests against the overall value and strategic direction of the product.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to manage stakeholder expectations.
explanation3: Incorrect: Managing the Product Backlog is the Product Owner’s responsibility, not the Scrum Master’s.
answer4: Ignore low-priority requests to focus only on urgent items.
explanation4: Incorrect: All requests should be evaluated fairly based on value, not urgency alone.

title: During the Sprint, a stakeholder requests to add a new feature that is high priority. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should add new requests to the Product Backlog, prioritize them accordingly, and manage stakeholder expectations without disrupting the current Sprint. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Add the feature to the current Sprint Backlog immediately.
explanation1: Incorrect: Adding new work mid-Sprint disrupts the Sprint Goal and team focus.
answer2: Discuss the request with the team and adjust the Sprint Goal if needed.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal should not be changed once the Sprint has started.
answer3: Add the feature to the Product Backlog and prioritize it for the next Sprint.
explanation3: Correct: The Product Owner should manage the Product Backlog and prioritize new work for future Sprints.
answer4: Ignore the request and continue with the current plan.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner should acknowledge the request and manage it appropriately.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take to ensure that the Product Backlog remains aligned with business objectives? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner should regularly engage with stakeholders and use data-driven prioritization to keep the Product Backlog aligned with evolving business objectives, maximizing value delivery. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Update the Product Backlog only during formal Scrum events like Sprint Planning and Review.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should be continuously refined and updated based on evolving needs.
answer2: Engage with stakeholders regularly to gather feedback and adjust the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Regular engagement helps ensure the Product Backlog reflects current business needs and priorities.
answer3: Use data-driven prioritization to keep the Backlog focused on high-impact work.
explanation3: Correct: Data-driven decisions help maintain a Product Backlog that delivers the most value to the business.
answer4: Ignore feedback that conflicts with the current Product Goal.
explanation4: Incorrect: All feedback should be considered to maintain a responsive and adaptable Product Backlog.
answer5: Delegate Product Backlog refinement to the Developers to save time.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner is responsible for managing and updating the Product Backlog.

title: During a Sprint, the Developers identify that an item in the Product Backlog lacks sufficient detail. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to refine unclear items, ensuring they are actionable and meet the team's understanding for future implementation. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Defer the item to a future Sprint to allow more time for refinement.
explanation1: Incorrect: Delaying work does not address the lack of clarity; refinement should happen as part of ongoing Backlog management.
answer2: Work with the Developers to refine the item immediately, ensuring it is clear and actionable.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement ensures that Product Backlog items are ready for implementation and understood by the team.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to clarify the item with the team.
explanation3: Incorrect: While the Scrum Master can facilitate, refinement is primarily the Product Owner's responsibility.
answer4: Remove the item from the Backlog if it is unclear.
explanation4: Incorrect: Removing an unclear but valuable item does not resolve the issue of insufficient detail.

title: Which three actions best demonstrate the role of the Scrum Master in supporting the Scrum Team? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master supports the Scrum Team by facilitating events, assisting the Product Owner with Backlog refinement, and coaching the team on self-management. “The Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum Team’s effectiveness.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Directing the Developers on what tasks to complete each day.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not direct the team’s daily work.
answer2: Facilitating Scrum events to ensure they are productive and effective.
explanation2: Correct: Facilitating Scrum events is a core responsibility of the Scrum Master.
answer3: Helping the Product Owner refine and prioritize the Product Backlog.
explanation3: Correct: The Scrum Master supports the Product Owner in managing the Backlog effectively.
answer4: Coaching the team on self-management and cross-functionality.
explanation4: Correct: Coaching the team helps them become more autonomous and effective.
answer5: Assigning tasks to team members to improve efficiency.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not assign tasks; the team manages their own work.

title: Which artifact in Scrum provides a transparent view of what has been completed and what is still needed to achieve the Product Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Backlog is a dynamic, ordered list that represents everything needed to achieve the Product Goal, providing a clear view of what is complete and what remains. “The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Sprint Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Backlog shows the plan for the current Sprint but does not reflect progress toward the Product Goal.
answer2: Product Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Product Backlog is an ordered list of everything needed to improve the product and achieve the Product Goal.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment shows what has been completed but does not provide visibility into what is still needed.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done ensures quality but does not provide a view of progress towards the Product Goal.

title: Which artifact provides transparency into what work is currently being done and how the team plans to achieve the Sprint Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog provides a clear and transparent view of what the team is working on during the Sprint, supporting alignment with the Sprint Goal. “The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog shows future work but does not provide visibility into the current Sprint’s progress.
answer2: Sprint Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Backlog provides a transparent view of the work planned for the Sprint and the team’s progress.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment reflects completed work but does not show current planning or progress.
answer4: Scrum Artifacts
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done sets quality standards but does not provide insight into current work progress.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is solely responsible for writing all Product Backlog items. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner manages the Product Backlog, but creating items can be a collaborative effort involving the entire Scrum Team. “The Product Owner may do the above work, or have the Developers do it. However, the Product Owner remains accountable.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog, but anyone in the Scrum Team can write items.
explanation2: Correct: While the Product Owner manages the Product Backlog, the Development Team and others can contribute to writing items.

title: During Sprint Planning, the team identifies that a high-priority item lacks sufficient detail. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to refine unclear items, ensuring they are ready for inclusion and execution within the Sprint. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Include the item as-is and hope the Developers can figure it out during the Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Including unclear items can lead to wasted effort and unmet Sprint Goals.
answer2: Work with the Developers to refine the item before it is included in the Sprint Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement ensures items are clear, actionable, and understood by the team, supporting successful delivery.
answer3: Move the item to the next Sprint to allow more time for refinement.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying high-priority work can impact value delivery and should be avoided if possible.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to facilitate the refinement of the item.
explanation4: Incorrect: While the Scrum Master can facilitate, the Product Owner is responsible for ensuring items are ready.

title: During the Sprint, the Developers identify a risk that could impact the Sprint Goal. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
