feedback: The Product Owner should collaborate with the Developers to address risks, ensuring that the Sprint remains aligned with its Goal. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the risk to maintain focus on current tasks.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring risks can lead to failure in meeting the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Work with the Developers to assess the risk and adjust the Sprint Backlog if necessary.
explanation2: Correct: Addressing risks helps ensure that the team can meet the Sprint Goal and deliver value.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to resolve the risk independently.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates, but the Product Owner should be involved in prioritization and adjustments.
answer4: Escalate the risk to management to find a solution.
explanation4: Incorrect: Risks should be managed within the Scrum Team without unnecessary escalation.

title: Which two actions should the Product Owner take when multiple Scrum Teams are working on the same product? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: When multiple teams work on the same product, the Product Owner must ensure coordination and effective management of the Product Backlog to maintain alignment and maximize value delivery. “Multiple Scrum Teams often work together on the same product.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Create separate Product Backlogs for each team to avoid conflicts.
explanation1: Incorrect: All teams should work from a single, unified Product Backlog to maintain alignment.
answer2: Facilitate regular communication between teams to ensure shared understanding of the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Regular communication helps avoid duplication and ensures teams are aligned.
answer3: Adjust priorities in the Product Backlog to manage dependencies between teams.
explanation3: Correct: Managing dependencies through prioritization helps streamline work across multiple teams.
answer4: Allow each team to independently manage their Backlog priorities.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should remain unified under the Product Owner’s guidance.
answer5: Delegate Backlog management to the Scrum Master to reduce workload.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Product Owner maintains responsibility for the entire Product Backlog.

title: Which three actions demonstrate effective Product Backlog management by the Product Owner? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Effective Product Backlog management involves continuous refinement, prioritization based on feedback and data, and collaboration with the team to ensure the Backlog reflects current needs and goals. “The Product Owner is accountable for effective Product Backlog management.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Delegating all refinement tasks to the Developers to save time.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner must actively participate in refinement and cannot delegate Backlog management entirely.
answer2: Regularly reprioritizing items based on feedback from stakeholders and market conditions.
explanation2: Correct: Regular reprioritization ensures the Backlog reflects current priorities and delivers maximum value.
answer3: Collaborating with the Developers to clarify and refine Product Backlog items continuously.
explanation3: Correct: Ongoing collaboration ensures items are clear, well understood, and actionable.
answer4: Using data and metrics to drive prioritization decisions.
explanation4: Correct: Data-driven prioritization aligns the Product Backlog with business goals and value delivery.
answer5: Waiting until Sprint Planning to adjust and refine the Product Backlog.
explanation5: Incorrect: Refinement and adjustments should be ongoing, not delayed until formal planning sessions.

title: Which two actions are critical for the Scrum Master to effectively facilitate Scrum events? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master facilitates effective events by ensuring preparation and maintaining time-boxing, allowing the team to stay focused and productive. “The Scrum Master ensures that Scrum events take place and are positive, productive, and kept within the time-box.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ensuring all team members are prepared for each event.
explanation1: Correct: Preparation ensures that the team can participate fully and that the event is productive and focused.
answer2: Keeping the events within the time-box to respect everyone’s time.
explanation2: Correct: Time-boxing ensures events are efficient and do not disrupt the team’s workflow.
answer3: Solving problems for the team during the event.
explanation3: Incorrect: The team should solve their own problems; the Scrum Master facilitates rather than solves.
answer4: Allowing events to extend if important discussions arise.
explanation4: Incorrect: Time-boxing should be respected to keep the events concise and focused.
answer5: Skipping events that seem unnecessary to save time.
explanation5: Incorrect: All Scrum events are important and serve specific purposes; skipping them undermines the Scrum framework.

title: Which two elements are essential for the Product Owner when prioritizing the Product Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner ensures the Product Backlog is prioritized effectively by regularly reviewing feedback and focusing on items with the highest potential impact and value. “The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Regularly reviewing and adjusting the Product Backlog based on stakeholder feedback.
explanation1: Correct: Continuous refinement based on feedback ensures that the Product Backlog remains relevant and valuable.
answer2: Assessing items based on their potential impact and business value.
explanation2: Correct: Prioritizing by impact and value ensures the most important work is done first, maximizing the product’s success.
answer3: Delegating prioritization decisions to the Development Team.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing value through prioritization, not the Development Team.
answer4: Setting the priority based solely on the technical complexity of items.
explanation4: Incorrect: Technical complexity is considered, but prioritization focuses primarily on value and impact.
answer5: Leaving low-value items at the top of the Backlog to address them first.
explanation5: Incorrect: High-value items should be prioritized to maximize product success and stakeholder satisfaction.

title: Midway through a Sprint, the team realizes they have misunderstood a key requirement, impacting the Sprint Goal. What should they do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Discussing the issue in the Daily Scrum and working with the Product Owner ensures that the team can adapt effectively and realign with the Sprint Goal. “During the Sprint, scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Continue with the Sprint as planned to avoid disruptions.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring the problem does not help achieve the Sprint Goal and may result in wasted effort.
answer2: Discuss the issue in the Daily Scrum and adapt the plan with input from the Product Owner.
explanation2: Correct: The Daily Scrum allows the team to adapt their plan and work closely with the Product Owner to address the misunderstanding.
answer3: Cancel the Sprint and start over.
explanation3: Incorrect: Cancelling the Sprint is extreme and not the best response to misunderstandings.
answer4: Blame the Product Owner for not clarifying requirements.
explanation4: Incorrect: Blaming does not resolve the issue or foster collaboration.

title: The team frequently fails to complete Product Backlog items due to a lack of refinement. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should work with the Developers to improve the refinement process, ensuring that Product Backlog items are properly prepared for selection in future Sprints. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Delay incomplete items to the next Sprint to give the team more time.
explanation1: Incorrect: Delaying items without refinement does not address the core issue of preparation.
answer2: Work with the Developers to improve the refinement process and ensure items are ready for selection.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement ensures that Product Backlog items are well-understood and actionable, reducing the likelihood of incomplete work.
answer3: Lower the standards of refinement to speed up the process.
explanation3: Incorrect: Lowering standards can compromise product quality and lead to misalignment with goals.
answer4: Ignore the issue and focus on completing the current Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: Ignoring refinement issues can cause recurring problems and impact future Sprints.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Development Team realizes that the scope of work may be too large to complete in one Sprint. What should they do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: If the scope seems too large, the Development Team should work with the Product Owner to adjust the scope, ensuring that the Sprint Goal remains realistic and achievable. “Sprint Planning initiates the Sprint by laying out the work to be performed.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Continue as planned and try to complete as much as possible.
explanation1: Incorrect: Starting with unrealistic expectations can lead to poor quality and unmet Sprint Goals.
answer2: Collaborate with the Product Owner to adjust the scope and ensure the Sprint Goal is achievable.
explanation2: Correct: Adjusting the scope with the Product Owner’s input helps the team set realistic expectations and stay aligned with the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Ignore the concern and proceed; the Scrum Master can resolve it later.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not make scope decisions; these should be addressed during Sprint Planning.
answer4: Extend the Sprint length to accommodate the extra work.
explanation4: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint is not allowed as it violates the time-boxing principle of Scrum.

title: True or False: Adaptation is a process that occurs only at the end of the Sprint during the Sprint Review. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Adaptation is not limited to the Sprint Review; it is a continuous process that happens whenever the team identifies necessary adjustments. “The Scrum Team is expected to adapt the moment it learns anything new.” Scrum Guide 2020
explanation1: Incorrect: Adaptation can occur whenever the team learns something new, not just during the Sprint Review.
explanation2: Correct: Adaptation occurs throughout the Sprint, whenever necessary, based on inspections.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies that they struggle with understanding the Product Backlog items. What should the Product Owner do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner should actively work with the Developers to refine Product Backlog items, ensuring they are clear, actionable, and ready for future Sprints. “Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog.” Scrum Guide 2020
answer1: Ignore the feedback and continue with the current refinement process.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring feedback can result in recurring misunderstandings and inefficiencies.
answer2: Collaborate with the Developers to improve refinement, ensuring items are clear and actionable.
explanation2: Correct: Enhancing refinement processes ensures items are well understood and reduces future misunderstandings.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to address refinement challenges independently.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner plays a key role in refinement and should be actively involved.
answer4: Delay addressing the feedback until the next Sprint Planning session.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement improvements should be made continuously, not delayed.
